#| message: false
source("../R/waning.R")
library(knitr)

## KG's rat equations

The rat equations in @keeling2000bubonic [eq. 2] are the same as those
in the Methods section of @keeling2000metapopulation:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{dS_R}{dt} &= r_R S_R\left(1 - \frac{T_R}{K_R}\right) + r_R R_R(1-p) - d_R S_R
   - \beta_R \frac{S_R}{T_R} F\left[1-e^{-aT_R}\right],\\
\frac{dI_R}{dt} &= \beta_R \frac{S_R}{T_R} F\left[1-e^{-aT_R}\right] - (d_R + m_R) I_R,\\
\frac{dR_R}{dt} &= r_R R_R\left(p - \frac{T_R}{K_R}\right) + m_R g_R I_R - d_R R_R,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $T_R = S_R + I_R + R_R$. The parameters are $r_R = 5$/yr,
$d_R = 0.2$/yr, $K_R = 2500$ and $p = 0.975$.

The term that looks odd is the recruitment of susceptibles born to
resistant parents, $r_R R_R(1-p)$. It has no density-dependent factor.
The density-dependent term $-r_R R_R T_R/K_R$ is charged entirely to
$R_R$.

Neither paper comments on this. @keeling2000bubonic only says that
"both susceptible and resistant rats breed with a net reproductive rate
of $r_R$ and a carrying capacity $K_R$; however, a proportion $p$ of the
offspring inherit resistance". @keeling2000metapopulation adds that "in
the absence of plague, the rat population experiences logistic growth,
with slowly waning resistance to the disease at the population level
governed by the parameter $p$".

## Two readings

**KG as written: density-dependent mortality.** Regroup the terms:

- births at the full rate $r_R$. $S_R$ offspring go to $S$. $R_R$
  offspring are split $p : (1-p)$ between $R$ and $S$.
- density-dependent mortality at per-capita rate $r_R T_R/K_R$ on $S_R$
  and $R_R$, but not on $I_R$.

On this reading the equations are internally consistent. The total
uninfected population $U = S_R + R_R$ still grows logistically.

**Density-dependent recruitment.** Births happen at per-capita rate
$b = r_R(1 - T_R/K_R)$, split as above. This is what the yersinia
stochastic model does (`inst/odin/plague_stochastic_humans.R`). It also
multiplies resistant fecundity by $\iota = 0.75$, which KG don't have.

With no disease, $U$ follows the same trajectory under both readings.
They differ only in how $U$ is split between $S$ and $R$.

## Dynamics of the resistant fraction

Let $f = R/(S+R)$ be the resistant fraction. With no disease, both
readings give

$$
f' = -(1-p)\, b(t)\, f ,
$$

where $b(t)$ is the per-capita birth rate. Each round of births leaks a
fraction $1-p$ of the resistant parents' offspring into $S$.

- **KG:** $b = r_R$, so $f$ decays at the constant rate $r_R(1-p)$
  (0.125/yr, half-life about 5.5 yr) whatever the population size.
- **Recruitment:** $b = r_R(1 - T/K)$. Since $U' = (b - d)U$, we have
  $\int b\,dt = \ln(T_\text{end}/T_0) + d\tau$ over an interval of
  length $\tau$, so

  $$
  \frac{f_\text{end}}{f_0} = \left(\frac{T_0}{T_\text{end}}\right)^{1-p} e^{-(1-p)\, d\, \tau}.
  $$

At the disease-free equilibrium $T^* = K(1 - d/r)$, the two readings
wane at very different rates:

| Where density dependence acts | Waning rate at $T^*$ | KG parameters |
|---|---|---|
| mortality (KG) | <span style="white-space: nowrap;">$r_R(1-p)$</span> | 0.125/yr (half-life ≈ 5.5 yr) |
| recruitment | <span style="white-space: nowrap;">$d_R(1-p)$</span> | 0.005/yr (half-life ≈ 140 yr) |

: Waning of resistance at the disease-free equilibrium.

The two readings also imply very different rat lifespans at $K$: about
$1/r_R \approx 2.4$ months (KG) versus $1/d_R = 5$ years (recruitment).

### The equilibrium comparison is misleading on its own

After a crash, $T \ll K$, so births are temporarily much faster under
the recruitment reading, which dilutes resistance while the population
regrows. But:

1. **The dilution is logarithmic in the depth of the crash and scaled by
   $1-p$.** With $p = 0.975$, even a 1000-fold crash only dilutes
   resistance by a factor of
   <span style="white-space: nowrap;">$1000^{0.025} \approx 1.19$.</span>
2. **The recruitment reading can never wane faster than KG along the
   same trajectory.** Since $r_R(1 - T/K) \le r_R$ at all times, the
   post-crash burst of births only brings it up toward the rate KG use
   all the time.
3. **Regrowth takes about a year at $r_R = 5$/yr.** During regrowth the
   two readings dilute resistance by similar amounts. They diverge in
   the years the population then spends near $K$, which dominate the
   inter-epidemic interval with KG's parameters.
4. **When $p$ is far from 1, regrowth dilution is large.** With
   $p = 0.5$, a 100-fold crash cuts resistance to about 10% through
   regrowth alone. This is probably why the yersinia metapopulation
   vignette (which uses the recruitment reading) needed $p = 0.5$ to
   get KG-like persistence.

### Numerical check

The table below gives the resistant fraction $f$ after a crash to a
fraction of $T^*$, starting with all survivors resistant ($f_0 = 1$).
It uses KG's demographic parameters and comes from `R/waning.R`. The
last column is the prediction for regrowth dilution alone under the
recruitment reading, (crash)$^{1-p}$.

```{r waning-table}
res <- waning_grid()
wide <- reshape(res, idvar = c("p", "crash", "time"),
                timevar = "version", direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^f\\.", "", names(wide))
wide$`regrowth pred.` <- regrowth_dilution(wide$p, wide$crash)
wide$`regrowth pred.`[wide$time != max(wide$time)] <- NA
kable(wide, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("p", "crash (× T*)", "t (yr)", "KG", "recruitment",
                    "regrowth pred."))
```

## Caveats

These results are for the disease-free dynamics only. With plague
present:

- epidemics selectively remove susceptibles, so $f_0$ after an epidemic
  is high but below 1;
- survivors of infection (fraction $g_R$) join $R$;
- low-level ongoing infection keeps pushing $f$ up.

Comparing the two readings properly needs the full model over complete
epidemic → crash → recovery → inter-epidemic cycles, across a range of
$p$. See the corresponding item in `TODO.md`. The location of density
dependence is a candidate for the most important parameter for
metapopulation persistence.

## Related problems in yersinia

- The deterministic KG reference vignette
  (`vignettes/reference-deterministic-models.Rmd`) copies KG's $S$/$R$
  equations exactly, but its flea-index equation leaves out $d_F$ (it
  uses $F[1-e^{-aT}]/T$ instead of $d_F F[1-e^{-aT}]/T$).
- The parameter documentation (`inst/explainer/build.R`) says values of
  $p$ near 1 "prevent the resistance trait from washing out". In KG,
  $1-p$ is what sets the rate at which resistance washes out.
  @keeling2000bubonic [Table 1] also cite Hirst (1938) for $p$, whereas
  the yersinia documentation says it has "no empirical basis".
